headline: Population structure as control parameter in epidemic threshold and coexistence models
label: Interaction Structure In Epidemic Dynamics
summary: Four recent preprints treat structure in phenology, spatial transport, behavior, and host networks as the explicit parameter governing model outcomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that a structural feature is carried explicitly into the model and serves as the variable that determines the outcome. The chemotaxis PDE framework for airborne transmission defines a spatially-aware reproduction number and pairs stabilized numerics with simulations for Lombardy and Georgia. HeSIR incorporates bimodal behavioral heterogeneity, derives a closed-form threshold, and maps the result onto an effective contact network. The multi-strain SIS model with coinfection in structured hosts uses a global replicator equation to link invasion fitness to coexistence. The tree-population study reduces a model with summer-dormancy thresholds to two ODEs and contrasts warming and drought effects. What is new across these preprints is the explicit treatment of structure as the control variable, applied across organisms and spatial scales.
